questions.stem: A solid wooden block has the shape of a right circular cylinder of radius 6 cm and height 9 cm. A conical hole with the same base radius and the same height is drilled out of the block. What fraction of the cylinder's volume remains?
questions.exp: Cone and cylinder share base and height, and the cone's volume is one third of the cylinder's, so 1 − 1/3 = 2/3 of the volume remains. The option 1/3 is the fraction removed, not the fraction left.

questions.stem: A circle of radius 5 cm is inscribed in a square. Taking π = 3.14, what is the area of the part of the square that lies outside the circle?
questions.exp: An inscribed circle touches all four sides, so the square has side 10 cm and area 100 cm², while the circle has area 3.14 × 5² = 78.5 cm²; the difference is 21.5 cm². The option 121.5 cm² adds the two areas instead of subtracting.
questions.topic: Maths · shaded areas (circle in a square)

questions.stem: An equilateral triangle has sides of length 12 cm. What is its area?
questions.exp: The height comes from the 30-60-90 half triangle: h = 6√3 cm, so the area is (1/2) × 12 × 6√3 = 36√3 cm². The option 72 cm² wrongly uses the side length 12 as the height.
questions.topic: Maths · equilateral triangle (area from the height)

questions.stem: A closed cylindrical tin has radius 3 cm and height 8 cm. What is its total surface area, ends included?
questions.exp: The two ends contribute 2πr² = 18π cm² and the curved wall contributes 2πrh = 48π cm², a total of 66π cm². The option 48π cm² counts only the wall and 57π cm² forgets one of the two ends.

questions.stem: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 3:40? (The hour hand turns at 0.5° per minute, the minute hand at 6° per minute.)
questions.exp: At 3:40 the hour hand is at 3 × 30 + 40 × 0.5 = 110° and the minute hand at 40 × 6 = 240°, both measured from 12, so the angle between them is 240 − 110 = 130°. The option 150° leaves the hour hand fixed at exactly 3, ignoring its 20° drift.

questions.stem: Between 7:00 and 8:00 the hands of a clock are exactly 100 degrees apart at 7:20. At what later time in that hour are they exactly 100 degrees apart again? (The hour hand turns at 0.5 degrees per minute, the minute hand at 6 degrees per minute.)
questions.exp: Measured from 12, the hour hand sits at 210 + 0.5m degrees and the minute hand at 6m, so the gap is 5.5m - 210. Setting the gap to 100 gives 5.5m = 110 (7:20) or 5.5m = 310, so m = 56 and 4/11 minutes. The 7:52 option answers a gap of 80 degrees (5.5m = 290), and 8:00 exactly is what a closing rate of 5 degrees per minute would give.

questions.stem: What is the value of tan 30° × tan 60°?
questions.exp: tan 30° = √3/3 and tan 60° = √3, so the product is (√3/3) × √3 = 3/3 = 1. The option 1/3 uses tan 30° twice, and 3 divides the two values instead of multiplying them.

questions.stem: For an angle θ, what is the value of (sin θ + cos θ)² − 2 sin θ cos θ?
questions.exp: Expanding the square gives sin²θ + 2 sinθ cosθ + cos²θ − 2 sinθ cosθ = sin²θ + cos²θ = 1. The option 2 sinθ cosθ stops after the expansion and forgets to cancel the middle term against the one subtracted.

questions.stem: What is the value of (sin 45° − cos 45°)² + 2 sin 30° cos 60°?
questions.exp: sin 45° = cos 45°, so the squared term is 0, and 2 sin 30° cos 60° = 2 × (1/2) × (1/2) = 1/2, giving 1/2 in total. The option 0 forgets the second term, and 1 overestimates the product sin 30° cos 60°.

questions.stem: A straight line passes through the points (2, 5) and (6, 17). What is its slope?
questions.exp: The slope is the change in y over the change in x: (17 − 5)/(6 − 2) = 12/4 = 3. The options 4 and 12 use only one of the two changes, and 1/3 inverts the ratio.

questions.stem: A cyclist rides along a straight road at a constant speed. Her distance from the start is recorded as 1.8 km after 6 minutes and 3.0 km after 10 minutes. What is her speed in m/s?
questions.exp: Between the two records she covers 1.2 km = 1200 m in 4 min = 240 s, so her speed is 1200/240 = 5 m/s. The option 18 m/s is the speed in km/h (0.3 km/min × 60) left unconverted, and 300 m/s keeps the rate in metres per minute without dividing by 60.
questions.topic: Maths · rate of change from data (unit conversion)

questions.stem: Water is pumped into a tank that already contains 40 L. The volume reaches 90 L after 5 minutes and 160 L after 15 minutes. What is the average rate of inflow over the whole 15 minutes?
questions.exp: The volume rises from 40 L to 160 L, a change of 120 L in 15 min, so the average rate is 8 L/min. The option 8.5 L/min averages the two segment rates (10 and 7 L/min) instead of dividing the total change by the total time.
